title: Buffer Preparation for OnePot PURE Cell-Free System
author: Konstantinos Ragios
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.728hqhw
materials: Add the materials needed the buffer you want to produce in a beaker. The final concentration of the components for the different buffers is presented in Table 1 and Table 2
Table 1 : Buffers for Protein Purification In Stock Buffer B, Glycerol should consists of 60% of the final volume
Table 2: Buffers for Ribosome Purification In Cusion buffer, Sucrose should consists of 30% of the final volume
The buffers are then stored at 4 o C

steps.title: Dissolve solids in water
steps.instruction: Add distilled water to the container and mix with a magnetic stirrer until all solid components are completely dissolved; avoid exceeding the desired intermediate volume to keep component concentrations correct.

steps.title: Adjust to final volume
steps.instruction: Add additional distilled water as needed to bring the buffer solution to its final intended volume.

steps.title: Filter buffer solution
steps.instruction: Pass the prepared buffer through an appropriate filter to remove any particulates.

steps.title: Store buffer at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Place the filtered buffer in a storage container and keep it at 4 °C until needed.

steps.title: Add fresh β‑mercaptoethanol
steps.instruction: Immediately before each experiment, add β‑mercaptoethanol to the buffer (its short half‑life requires fresh addition each time).
